text:
Predicates:
SpillsFoodClothing(x) ::: x spills a lot of food on his clothing.
NotablyTidy(x) ::: x is notably tidy.
ClumsyFoodie(x) ::: x is a clumsy foodie.
GoesOutFrequent(x) ::: x goes out frequently to find new food restaurants.
People(x) ::: x is a person.
Cleanly(x) ::: x is cleanly.
ValuessOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x values order and spotlessness.
FamilyPrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x's family prioritizes order and spotlessness.
Peter(x) ::: x is Peter.
---
Premises:
∀x (SpillsFoodClothing(x) → ¬NotablyTidy(x)) ::: If people spill a lot of food on their clothing, then they are not notably tidy.
∀x (ClumsyFoodie(x) ∧ GoesOutFrequent(x) → SpillsFoodClothing(x)) ::: All clumsy foodies who go out frequently spill a lot of food on their clothing.
∀x (Cleanly(x) → NotablyTidy(x)) ::: If people are cleanly, then they are notably tidy.
∀x (ValuessOrderAndSpotlessness(x) → Cleanly(x)) ::: If people value order and spotlessness, then they are cleanly.
∀x (FamilyPrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) → ValuessOrderAndSpotlessness(x)) ::: All people whose families prioritize order and spotlessness value order and spotlessness.
Peter(x) → ( (SpillsFoodClothing(x) ∧ Cleanly(x)) ∨ (¬SpillsFoodClothing(x) ∧ ¬Cleanly(x)) ) ::: Peter is either a person who spills food and is cleanly, or a person who does not spill food and is not cleanly.
---
Conclusion:
IsPeterNotablyTidy(x) ::: Whether Peter is notably tidy or not is uncertain based on the premises.
